blocks.value: The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is a momentum indicator that helps traders understand whether a stock may be overbought or oversold.
Imagine This: If you sprint continuously for a long distance, you'll eventually become tired and slow down. Similarly, when a stock rises too quickly, it may pause or fall before continuing.
RSI ranges from 0 to 100. Traditionally, values above 70 indicate that a stock may be overbought, while values below 30 suggest it may be oversold.
⚠️ Overbought does not always mean the price will immediately fall, and oversold does not guarantee it will rise.
If RSI reaches 75 after a strong rally, traders may become cautious and look for additional confirmation before buying.
Never use RSI alone. Combine it with trends and support/resistance.
